note: Written by Claude from reputable outlets (Reuters via syndication partners, Bloomberg, SCMP, ABC News, The Korea Herald, Japan Times, Nippon.com/Jiji, The Week, WION, TechCrunch, The Washington Post and others); source under each story. Sunday news flow was light and several outlets could not be retrieved, so some sections are shorter rather than padded. Disclosure: Claude is made by Anthropic, which appears in today's news. Sports excluded.

items.headline: Binance restarts withdrawals after clawing back most of $6.3bn hack
items.summary: Binance began restoring withdrawals in phases, starting with bitcoin and ether, after recovering about 95% of the $6.3bn in tokens stolen last week, Reuters reports.

items.headline: FBI pins record Binance theft on North Korea
items.summary: The FBI attributed the theft to North Korea's TraderTraitor hacking unit, the same group it blamed for the $1.5bn Bybit hack in 2025. It would be the largest single crypto heist on record.

items.headline: DeepSeek open-sources a more autonomous coding agent
items.summary: China's DeepSeek released Super-Agent, a research prototype of a coding agent, as open source, pitching it as a challenger to Anthropic's Claude Code.

items.headline: Google's first data-centre satellite is up and running
items.summary: Google says its Suncatcher prototype, launched on October 1, is online and talking to ground stations; its onboard Gemma 4 model even composed a haiku about orbit.

items.headline: A crowded week: midterms, jobs data and rate-hike bets
items.summary: After disappointing results from Alphabet, Amazon and Intel hit shares, investors face US midterms on Tuesday and the October jobs report on Friday. Markets were pricing roughly an 80% chance of a Fed hike in December, according to Reuters; September payrolls rose just 29,000.

items.headline: Binance discloses $3.6bn in net outflows after the theft
items.summary: Bloomberg reports Binance saw $3.6bn of net customer outflows following the hack as it reopens withdrawals in phases.

items.headline: Australian home prices on track for steepest slump in 40 years
items.summary: Australian house prices fell for a seventh straight month in October, the fastest pace of decline in four decades, according to Cotality data reported by the ABC.

items.headline: Singapore targets energy-hungry air-conditioners
items.summary: The SCMP examines Singapore's push to curb power-hungry air-conditioners.

items.headline: Quad leaders to meet in Manila ahead of Trump–Xi talks
items.summary: Quad foreign ministers meeting in Atlanta finalised the group's first leaders' summit in two years, set for Manila. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio insisted the Quad is not anti-China.

items.headline: Malaysia's Loke rejects school alcohol claims as a political attack
items.summary: Transport Minister Anthony Loke denied that students were made to serve alcohol at a school reunion dinner; police are still investigating.

items.headline: EV boom leaves local parts makers behind
items.summary: Auto parts suppliers in Indonesia, Thailand and Malaysia are seeing demand fall as Chinese carmakers lean on their own supply chains.

items.headline: Filipinos abroad mark Undas far from home
items.summary: Millions of overseas Filipino workers face the strain of honouring their dead from afar during Undas, the two-day All Saints' and All Souls' observance.

items.headline: Region's graduates fear AI is eating entry-level jobs
items.summary: From Bangkok to Singapore, young jobseekers say AI is thinning the pool of graduate roles.

items.headline: Takaichi calls for calm in Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb
items.summary: In a video message to the Manama Dialogue in Bahrain, PM Sanae Takaichi urged early stability in both straits and pledged to work with Gulf states to keep sea lanes open. She is the first Japanese PM to address the forum this way.

items.headline: Tax-free shopping switches to 'pay now, refund later'
items.summary: From November 1, tourists pay full tax-inclusive prices and claim refunds through customs on departure. Goods must be bought within 90 days of leaving, with no spending cap.

items.headline: GMO chief to brief press on cyberattack
items.summary: GMO Internet Group CEO Masatoshi Kumagai will hold a news conference on Monday about the cyberattack on the company.

items.headline: Opposition wants Takaichi in the room for tax-cut debate
items.summary: Opposition parties are demanding the prime minister attend Diet deliberations as debate continues on the government's tax-cut bill.

items.headline: Erdogan and Ramos-Horta to visit Seoul this week
items.summary: Turkey's Recep Tayyip Erdogan makes a state visit November 2–4 with a summit on the 3rd; East Timor's Jose Ramos-Horta follows November 5–7, with talks and MOU signings on the 6th.

items.headline: Row over President Lee's social-media posts escalates
items.summary: Lee used X to defend his overseas trips; the opposition People Power Party called the posts emotional and noted the 2027 presidential travel budget is more than double this year's.

items.headline: Samsung's Lee Jae-yong tours Yokohama packaging lab
items.summary: On his first visit since it opened in September, the Samsung chair stressed advanced packaging for AI chips. Samsung plans to invest 350bn won (about $262m) in the lab through 2028.

items.headline: 4.4 million North Korean probes hit Korean financial firms
items.summary: Since October 21, authorities have detected about 4.4 million scanning attempts from North Korean IP addresses against local financial institutions, though no breach is confirmed.

items.headline: Seven in 10 Koreans report mental health problems
items.summary: A National Center for Mental Health survey found 70.1% of South Koreans experienced mental health issues in the past year.

items.headline: National gun buyback opens today
items.summary: A year-long buyback starts on November 2, but so far only NSW and the ACT have signed up.

items.headline: ASIC threatens super funds over complaints
items.summary: The corporate regulator says super funds are failing members and warns of legal action against those that do not resolve complaints.

items.headline: One in four young men say violence for a cause can be justified
items.summary: A democracy survey finds trust in politicians falling, though confidence in key institutions remains high.

items.headline: Algal bloom killed more than 8,000 sharks and rays
items.summary: A citizen-science report estimates the toll and suggests some species may have been pushed close to extinction.

items.headline: Government under pressure before expected rate rise
items.summary: ABC analysis says Labor must show unity and a clear plan ahead of the interest-rate rise widely expected from the RBA on Tuesday.

items.headline: Judge throws out DOJ bid to stall Alaska Senate result
items.summary: A judge dismissed the Justice Department lawsuit seeking to block certification if Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan loses to Democrat Mary Peltola; the suit centred on a second 'Sullivan' on the ranked-choice ballot.

items.headline: Trump stumps in Iowa and Kansas in final weekend
items.summary: Two days before the midterms, Trump campaigned in states he won in 2024, as Speaker Mike Johnson predicted Republicans would beat expectations despite polls showing Democratic momentum.

items.headline: Chatbots lean on obscure AI-built voter sites
items.summary: Washington Post testing found chatbots drew midterm answers from three little-known AI-generated sites; Copilot cited the error-prone Ballot Brief in 75% of tests and ChatGPT in 22%.

items.headline: G20 foreign ministers leave Atlanta without consensus
items.summary: The meeting hosted by the US ended without agreement on key issues.

items.headline: Ex-Sinopec and CNOOC boss Fu Chengyu under graft probe
items.summary: The anti-graft commission is investigating Fu, 75, for serious violations of discipline and law, Xinhua said.

items.headline: Beijing hits back at US ban on Chinese testing labs
items.summary: The commerce ministry urged Washington to revoke an FCC rule, taking effect in December 2028, barring all Chinese labs from certifying US-bound devices. FCC chair Brendan Carr said 82% of electronics were tested in China in 2025.

items.headline: Quad voices concern over 'overcapacity'
items.summary: Without naming China, Quad foreign ministers flagged overcapacity disrupting supply chains, even as Rubio said the group is not aimed at Beijing.

items.headline: Tougher route into elite cadre scheme for overseas graduates
items.summary: China is narrowing access to an elite official training programme for returnees, adding to pressure from a shrinking civil-service intake.

items.headline: Study warns AI could turn social credit into surveillance
items.summary: Researchers say algorithmic tracking of online and offline behaviour could make the social credit system a surveillance tool and drive discrimination.

items.headline: INDIA bloc rallies in Delhi against voter-roll revision
items.summary: The opposition rallied at Ramlila Maidan against the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls and demanded the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar; Akhilesh Yadav alleged 1.27 crore deleted voters were Hindus. The BJP called the rally a flop.

items.headline: Opposition protest movements converge on Modi
items.summary: Bloomberg reports India's protest movements are uniting, posing a fresh political headache for the prime minister.

items.headline: Ashutosh Dixit takes over as Air Force chief
items.summary: The test pilot, with over 3,500 flying hours, became India's 29th Chief of Air Staff on October 31, succeeding Amar Preet Singh.

items.headline: Modi to open renewable energy summit with 130 countries
items.summary: The prime minister is set to launch the Global Renewable Energy Summit in Delhi, with 130 nations taking part, UNI reports.
